transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’ve just taken on too much lately—projects, workshops, fixing up the studio, calls with clients. More than I can really handle. And now the deadlines… and the mortgage… it’s starting to feel like it’s catching up with me.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or wired compared with your normal self?

Yes… I suppose so. Most days I felt kind of unusually bright, energized—like everything in the studio and garden was finally coming together. But I was also… touchy. If someone questioned what I was doing, or brought up invoices, I could get sharp pretty quickly.
During that energized time, did you need much less sleep than usual?
I don’t really know. I mean, I was staying up later sometimes, but I’m not sure it was… much less than usual.
During that energized time, did you feel unusually confident or more capable than you normally do?

Yes… I did. I felt like my illustration work could become something much bigger, like a kind of visual language scientific journals had been missing. And I was… strangely sure I was the one who could do it.
During that energized time, were you talking more than usual?

Yes… I think so. In meetings I’d catch myself going on—faster than usual—about layouts and pigments and budgets, all tangled together. People had to stop me sometimes because I wasn’t really leaving room for them to answer.
During that energized time, were you more driven than usual to start or take on projects?
Yes. I was taking on… too much, really. More projects, workshops, fixing up the studio, client calls—things I couldn’t actually keep up with. Now the deadlines and the mortgage are… pressing in.
During that energized period, did it cause serious problems in your life or work?

Yes… it did. My illustration deadlines started slipping, and people at work had to keep checking in on me. I’d taken on too much, and spent money I should’ve kept aside for the studio… so now the mortgage is in a bad place.
During that energized time, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?
I’m not sure. I mean… I was thinking about a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call it racing. It’s hard to say.
During that energized time, were you more easily distracted than usual?
Yes… I think so. I’d sit down to finish a contract plate, and then some small thing—a bird at the window, or a catalog, or an idea for a workshop—would pull me away completely.
About how many days did that unusually energized period last?
About three months, I think… since I took on the mortgage for the cottage-studio.
During that energized period, did you have any experiences where you heard or saw things other people didn’t, or believed something that others said wasn’t true?

I didn’t see things, no. But… I did get very sure that a couple of clients, and even an editor, were trying to get into my sketches before I showed the system. People told me that wasn’t happening, but I couldn’t really let it go.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a sustained elevated/irritable energized period lasting about three months with multiple manic symptoms: increased confidence/grandiosity, pressured/excessive speech, increased goal-directed activity, distractibility, and significant functional impairment including missed deadlines and financial consequences. In addition, psychotic symptoms were present in the form of fixed suspicious/paranoid beliefs that clients/editor were trying to access sketches despite reassurance otherwise. This supports bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms.
